title: State Department Title VIII Research Program Loses Federal Funding in 2013
description_short: The State Department’s Title VIII program for Eurasian and Eastern European language training and research lost its FY2013 appropriation.
description_medium: In 2013, the State Department’s Title VIII program for language training and research in Eurasian and Eastern European studies did not receive an appropriation for the federal fiscal year ending September 30. Contemporary reporting said the loss reduced fellowships and grants available in 2013–14. The evidence does not connect this Obama-era funding decision to Donald Trump.
description_long: In October 2013, Inside Higher Ed reported that Title VIII, a State Department program supporting language training and research in Eurasian and Eastern European studies, did not receive an appropriation for the federal fiscal year ending September 30. The Association for Slavic, East European and Eurasian Studies said the absence would reduce fellowships and grants available in 2013–14. The article reported that Title VIII funding averaged about $4.5 million annually in the early 2000s and had been cut to $3.3 million in fiscal year 2012. A 2014 PONARS Eurasia republication of Alexander Gabuev’s Guardian article says State Department leadership decided in fall 2013 not to allocate money for Russian studies after Congress changed the relevant budget wording from “shall” to “may.” Together, the reports support a narrow account of a 2013 funding decision. They do not support the original claim that cuts continued through 2015 to shift resources toward Syria, ISIS, and gun violence. The decision predates Donald Trump’s presidency, and the evidence reviewed establishes no connection to him. Whether this unrelated Obama-era event belongs in a Trump-focused collection remains an editorial scope question.
date_precision: year; source identifies the FY2013 appropriation and reports fall 2013 decision, not an exact action day

source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The Association for Slavic, East European and Eurasian Studies (ASEEES) has learned that the Title VIII program – a U.S. State Department program that funds language training and research in Eurasian and Eastern European studies – did not receive an appropriation for the federal fiscal year that ended Sept. 30. Because the money is typically allocated one year and spent the next, that means a significant reduction in the number of fellowships and grants available in 2013-14.

children.title: Trump Declares a National Emergency at the Southern Border
children.description_short: A January 20, 2025 proclamation declared a southern-border emergency and directed military support for border operations.
children.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a proclamation declaring a national emergency at the U.S. southern border. The text invokes emergency and military authorities and directs the Defense Department to support Homeland Security with personnel, logistics, and additional barriers. It records the administration’s stated actions, not proof that each measure was implemented or that the proclamation’s factual assertions were accurate.
children.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a proclamation declaring a national emergency at the U.S. southern border. The text invokes sections of the National Emergencies Act and makes military authorities available, including provisions under Title 10, sections 12302 and 2808. It directs the Department of Defense to support the Department of Homeland Security through personnel, detention space, transportation, logistics, and additional physical barriers. The proclamation states these measures are intended to help the federal government obtain operational control of the border. This entry records the declaration and its stated directives; the text alone does not show which measures were implemented or their effects. It also does not establish the accuracy of the proclamation’s claims about conditions at the border. The original held item incorrectly presented this as one omnibus emergency covering immigration, energy, and economic policy and asserted that it bypassed environmental, safety, and notice-and-comment requirements. The national energy emergency appears in a separate presidential action issued on the same date, and the supplied documents do not support the broader bypass claim.

source_fact_map.fact: Trump’s proclamation declares a national emergency at the southern border and invokes statutory emergency authority.
source_fact_map.quote: hereby declare that a national emergency exists at the southern border of the United States
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: NOW, THEREFORE, I, DONALD J. TRUMP, President of the United States of America, by the authority vested in me by the Constitution and the laws of the United States of America, including sections 201 and 301 of the National Emergencies Act (50 U.S.C. 1601 et seq.), hereby declare that a national emergency exists at the southern border of the United States, and that section 12302 of title 10, United States Code, is invoked and made available, according to its terms, to the Secretaries of the military departments concerned, subject to the direction of the Secretary of Defense.

source_fact_map.fact: The proclamation directs Defense to support Homeland Security’s border operations with military resources and logistics.
source_fact_map.quote: shall order as many units or members of the Armed Forces, including the Ready Reserve and the National Guard
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Section 1. Deployment of Personnel and Resources. The Secretary of Defense, or the Secretary of each relevant military department, as appropriate and consistent with applicable law, shall order as many units or members of the Armed Forces, including the Ready Reserve and the National Guard, as the Secretary of Defense determines to be appropriate to support the activities of the Secretary of Homeland Security in obtaining complete operational control of the southern border of the United States.

children.title: Trump Declares a National Energy Emergency
children.description_short: A separate January 20, 2025 order declared an energy emergency and directed agencies to use lawful authorities to advance domestic energy resources.
children.description_medium: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a separate order declaring a national energy emergency. The order cites asserted shortfalls in energy supply and directs agencies to identify and use lawful emergency and other authorities to facilitate domestic energy resources. The document establishes the declaration and its stated rationale, not the accuracy of its claims or the implementation and effects of its directives.
children.description_long: On January 20, 2025, President Donald Trump issued a separate executive order declaring a national energy emergency. The order cites asserted shortfalls in domestic energy production, transportation, refining, and generation and directs agencies to identify and exercise lawful emergency authorities, along with other lawful powers, to facilitate the identification, leasing, siting, production, transportation, refining, and generation of domestic energy resources. It describes energy supply and grid reliability as matters of economic and national security. This entry covers the specific energy action and its stated purpose; it does not verify the administration’s characterization of an energy emergency, show that every directed action was implemented, or quantify resulting changes to energy production, prices, or infrastructure. The original held item merged this order with a separate southern-border proclamation and characterized the combined action as bypassing environmental, safety, and notice-and-comment rules. The sources support two distinct declarations but do not substantiate that broad legal characterization. This copy therefore retains only what the energy order says and keeps its stated rationales attributed to the administration.

source_fact_map.fact: Trump’s January 20 order declares a national energy emergency.
source_fact_map.quote: In light of these findings, I hereby declare a national emergency.
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: The United States’ insufficient energy production, transportation, refining, and generation constitutes an unusual and extraordinary threat to our Nation’s economy, national security, and foreign policy. In light of these findings, I hereby declare a national emergency.

source_fact_map.fact: The order directs agencies to use lawful authorities to facilitate domestic energy resources.
source_fact_map.quote: shall identify and exercise any lawful emergency authorities available to them, as well as all other lawful authorities they may possess
source_fact_map.source_excerpt: Sec. 2. Emergency Approvals. (a) The heads of executive departments and agencies (“agencies”) shall identify and exercise any lawful emergency authorities available to them, as well as all other lawful authorities they may possess, to facilitate the identification, leasing, siting, production, transportation, refining, and generation of domestic energy resources, including, but not limited to, on Federal lands.
